scenes.headline: How AngelSpec drafts per workload and shares verification
scenes.sub: Tencent's production speculative decoding: one drafter per workload, one budget per batch.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Gluon! AngelSpec is a production speculative decoding system: a cheap drafter proposes, the big model verifies. Here's what it changes.

scenes.text: Train a different drafter for each workload, and treat the target model's verification depth as a budget the whole batch shares.
scenes.mark: a budget the whole batch shares
scenes.say: The idea: a different drafter for each workload, and verification depth treated as a budget the whole batch shares.

left.title: Chat: an MTP drafter
items: High entropy: the next tokens are hard to guess
One block reused at increasing depth
left.say: Chat is hard to guess, so it gets a multi-token-prediction drafter, trained on its own predictions.

right.title: Code and math: DFly
items: A whole block drafted in one shot
Strengthened with code and math data
right.say: Code and math are nearly deterministic, so they get DFly, which drafts a whole block at once.

steps.say: DFly reads hidden states from several depths of the frozen target model.
Its draft blocks propose a whole block of tokens in parallel. That's the speed.
But a one-shot draft is blind to the token just chosen. A small head folds it back in.
Only that head runs in sequence, and the target still verifies, so the output is unchanged.

steps.label: Verify every drafted token
steps.say: Verifying costs roughly an order of magnitude more than drafting. Checking every draft for every request is the expensive default.

steps.label: Keep a batch-wide top slice by confidence
steps.note: keep ratio 0.25 to 1.0, picked by a profiled latency table
steps.say: D-cut flattens every drafted position in the batch, ranks them by the drafter's confidence, and keeps a global top slice. Confident requests keep more.

scenes.label: throughput from D-cut on replayed live traffic, at concurrency 64
scenes.note: for a 2.8% cost in accepted length, on H20 GPUs
scenes.say: On replayed live traffic, D-cut keeps rising where DFly flattens: fifteen point seven percent more throughput at concurrency sixty-four, for a two point eight percent cost in accepted length.

scenes.text: Don't ship one universal answer: match the drafter to the workload, and spend verification where the batch is most confident.
scenes.mark: where the batch is most confident

recap: An MTP drafter for chat, DFly for code
A small head makes a parallel draft causal
D-cut shares verification across the batch
scenes.say: To recap: two drafters, a cheap causal patch, and a verification budget the whole batch shares.
